name: sed
description: A stream editor that transforms text: substitution, deletion, insertion, and line selection, applied line by line.

flags.description: Substitute: replaces the first occurrence of old per line; add g for all occurrences.
Edit files in place (optionally with a backup suffix: -i.bak).
Suppress automatic printing; use with p to print selected lines.

examples.explanation: Prints file.txt with the first "hello" on each line replaced by "world" — the original file is unchanged without -i.
Edits the file in place, changing the SSH port. Keep a backup for important configs: sed -i.bak.
Replaces every occurrence on every line and writes the result to a new file.
Deletes comment lines (starting with #) and empty lines — a quick way to see the effective configuration.
Reorders ISO dates (2025-01-12 becomes 12.01.2025) using capture groups.

about: sed processes input one line at a time through an editing script. The s command is by far the most used: s/PATTERN/REPLACEMENT/FLAGS. Delimiters can be any character — s|/old/path|/new/path|g avoids escaping slashes. & in the replacement inserts the whole match; \1..\9 insert capture groups.
useCases: Strip comments and blank lines from configs.
Extract specific line ranges from large files.
mistakes: Forgetting to quote the expression: unquoted s/old/new/ lets the shell misinterpret slashes.
Using -i on a file you also read in the same pipeline — results are undefined.
warnings: sed -i rewrites the file and can destroy it on a bad expression. Test on a copy or use the backup suffix first.
distroNotes: GNU sed allows -i without a suffix; BSD/macOS sed requires -i ''. Scripts intended for both need sed -i '' on BSD.
